sensitive_terms: A pure-Python, bring-your-own-I/O implementation of HTTP/1.1
This is a little HTTP/1.1 library written from scratch in Python

runner.install_command: export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive && apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-pip && printf '[global]\nbreak-system-packages = true\n' > /etc/pip.conf && python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages --disable-pip-version-check 'setuptools==75.8.0' 'pytest==8.3.5' 'pytest-cov==6.0.0' && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
runner.env_probe_command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "import os; import httpwire; assert os.path.realpath(httpwire.__file__).startswith(os.path.realpath('httpwire')); client = httpwire.Connection(our_role=httpwire.CLIENT); wire = client.send(httpwire.Request(method='GET', target='/probe', headers=[('Host', 'localhost')])); assert wire.startswith(b'GET /probe HTTP/1.1'); assert client.send(httpwire.EndOfMessage()) == b''; server = httpwire.Connection(our_role=httpwire.SERVER); server.receive_data(wire); event = server.next_event(); assert type(event) is httpwire.Request and event.method == b'GET' and event.target == b'/probe'"

init_metadata.tech_stack: Pure Python bring-your-own-I/O HTTP/1.1 protocol state machine (setuptools flat layout, zero runtime deps, pytest); CPU-only
